## Concepts and intutions {.unnumbered}

Once, a colleague gave a lecture on Lotka-Volterra equation to undergraduate students in the biology department, when a student asked: "what is alpha?", she spent a few minutes explaining what alpha represented until another student interjected and said: "it is the one like the fish". She wake up call that understanding greek letter is a problem. And to the majority it is the case, so let's clear that out.

Do you recognize this? $(\zeta  + \xi)^2 = \zeta^2 + \xi^2 + 2\zeta\xi$

After staring for a while, one might realize that this is identité remarquable. In fact it exactly the same as $(a + b) ^ 2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab$.

This is the same as $13 + 9 = 22$ But this is the same as $XIII + IX = XXII$.

The romans were not great with math notations.

Eventually, it is a matter of notation, is there a reason to use roman letter in and only in the bible? Maybe because it clearly separate,

Likewise, using greek letter has a convience, and as with roman numbers, you just need to learn them and understand them. Not need to use them

## Formal {.unnumbered}

The only thing is just to learn the alphabet so here a quick summary There are upper and lower case. Here is the raw Markdown table formatted with explicit LaTeX syntax for the Greek characters, exactly as requested for easy copy-pasting:

| Lower Case | Upper Case | Latin Equivalent | Name    |
|:-----------|:-----------|:-----------------|:--------|
| $\alpha$   | $A$        | a                | Alpha   |
| $\beta$    | $B$        | b                | Beta    |
| $\gamma$   | $\Gamma$   | g                | Gamma   |
| $\delta$   | $\Delta$   | d                | Delta   |
| $\epsilon$ | $E$        | e                | Epsilon |
| $\zeta$    | $Z$        | z                | Zeta    |
| $\eta$     | $H$        | e                | Eta     |
| $\theta$   | $\Theta$   | th               | Theta   |
| $\iota$    | $I$        | i                | Iota    |
| $\kappa$   | $K$        | k                | Kappa   |
| $\lambda$  | $\Lambda$  | l                | Lambda  |
| $\mu$      | $M$        | m                | Mu      |
| $\nu$      | $N$        | n                | Nu      |
| $\xi$      | $\Xi$      | x                | Xi      |
| $\omicron$ | $O$        | o                | Omicron |
| $\pi$      | $\Pi$      | p                | Pi      |
| $\rho$     | $R$        | r                | Rho     |
| $\sigma$   | $\Sigma$   | s                | Sigma   |
| $\tau$     | $T$        | t                | Tau     |
| $\upsilon$ | $\Upsilon$ | y                | Upsilon |
| $\phi$     | $\Phi$     | ph               | Phi     |
| $\chi$     | $X$        | ch               | Chi     |
| $\psi$     | $\Psi$     | ps               | Psi     |
| $\omega$   | $\Omega$   | o                | Omega   |

## Tips and warning {.unnumbered}

epsilon and omicron iota etc are something small Omega is used as a set in maths and ohm in physics

Notation for birth is beta and death is delta, or mortality is mu, tau is time. Of course, you can but using something intuitive helps.
